The most recent PostgreSQL minor releases I found are 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24, and PostgreSQL 19 has reached release candidate 1.

- **Latest minor releases:** The project shipped an update to all supported versions of PostgreSQL, including 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, and 14.24, as well as the third beta release of PostgreSQL 19. That release skipped the 18.4 to 18.6 range, because 18.5 was not shipped due to a regression.
- **PostgreSQL 19:** The versioning page lists October 15, 2026: PostgreSQL 19 RC 1 Released!
- **Support policy:** A major version is supported for 5 years after its initial release. Minor releases come at least once every three months.
- **Supported status:** The versioning page marks 18, 17, 16, 15, and 14 as supported. Version 14's final release is listed as November 12, 2026, so it reaches end-of-life in about a month. Versions 13 and older are unsupported.

The versioning page's table metadata is dated about 917 days ago, so its minor-version numbers may be stale. The release announcements are more recent, so I'd treat 18.6 as the current minor release, but check the official site for anything newer.

content.text:
As of today (2026-10-17), the newest stable PostgreSQL is **18.x, and 18.6 is the latest minor release I found**. The search results were a bit inconsistent, so check the exact tag on Docker Hub.

- **Stable minors:** 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19 and 14.24 came out together in the same release. That release also included 19 Beta 3.
- **PostgreSQL 19:** It's at release candidate 1 (announced October 15, 2026). It isn't GA yet, so don't move production images to it.
- **PostgreSQL 14:** Its final release is listed as November 12, 2026, so it is about a month from end-of-life. Versions 13 and older are already unsupported.

**For your Docker image:**
- If you're on `postgres:18`, pin or pull `postgres:18.6` (or just rebuild with `--pull` if you track `18`).
- If you're on 17, 16 or 15, you're still supported. Just make sure you're on the latest minor, which is 17.11, 16.15 or 15.19.
- If you're on 14 or older, plan a major upgrade soon.
- A major upgrade needs `pg_upgrade` or dump/restore. You can't swap the image tag over an existing data directory.

The versioning page's table looked stale, and the search summary was a bit garbled. I'd treat 18.6 as current but confirm it before pinning. I can check your Dockerfile or compose files for the current tag if you point me at them. This directory isn't a git repo, so I haven't looked at any files yet.

Sources:
- [PostgreSQL: Versioning Policy](https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/)
- [PostgreSQL 18.6, 17.11, 16.15, 15.19, 14.24 and 19 Beta 3 Released!](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/postgresql-186-1711-1615-1519-1424-and-19-beta-3-released-3365/)
